function.name: check_smiles_reaction_template_matching
function.description: Checks if the SMARTS of a reaction template matches any substructure in the given SMILES.

smiles.description: SMILES string of the molecule to check.
smiles.title: Smiles

function.name: search_template_catalog_by_criteria
function.description: Searches the retrosynthetic template database based on specified criteria. The search criteria refer to the forward reaction.

molecule_smiles.description: SMILES string of the target molecule.
molecule_smiles.title: Molecule Smiles

functional_groups_broken.description: List of functional groups that are broken in the forward reaction. None will result in not filtering with this criterion.
functional_groups_broken.title: Functional Groups Broken

functional_groups_formed.description: List of functional groups that are formed in the forward reaction. None will result in not filtering with this criterion.
functional_groups_formed.title: Functional Groups Formed

bonds_formed.description: List of bonds that are formed in the forward reaction (e.g., "6-6", "6-8"). None will result in not filtering with this criterion.
bonds_formed.title: Bonds Formed

bonds_broken.description: List of bonds that are broken in the forward reaction (e.g., "6-6", "6-8"). None will result in not filtering with this criterion.
bonds_broken.title: Bonds Broken

bonds_order_changed.description: List of bonds whose order is changed in the forward reaction (e.g., "6-6 (1.0->2.0)"). None will result in not filtering with this criterion.
bonds_order_changed.title: Bonds Order Changed

limit.description: Maximum number of templates to return. Default is 10.
limit.title: Limit

Let me understand the task. I need to propose a retrosynthesis route for the molecule:
O=S(NC1=CC(N2CCN(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)CC2)=C3C(CCC4(CCC4)O3)=C1)(C5=C(F)C=CC=C5)=O

The route must have 6 reactions, and I'm given hints about what those reactions are (in forward direction):

1. Aromatic amine attacks phenylsulfonyl chloride to form sulfonamide (N-S bond formed, S-Cl bond broken)
2. Reduction of nitro to amine (nitro to primary amine, O-N bond broken)
3. Nucleophilic Aromatic Substitution (S_NAr) - nucleophile replaces halogen on aromatic ring (C-N bond formed, C-halogen bond broken)
4. Electrophilic Bromination - H on aromatic ring replaced by Br (C-Br bond formed, halide group formed)
5. Wolff-Kishner reduction - ketone to alkane (O-H bond of ketone broken, ketones functional group broken)
6. Cyclization of chalcones to flavanones - intramolecular Michael addition (C-C and C-O bonds formed, C-O bond broken, ether oxygens formed, aromatic hydroxyls and ketones broken)

Since these are forward reactions, I need to work backwards in retrosynthesis.

Let me start by analyzing the target molecule structure:
- It has a sulfonamide group (N-S(=O)2)
- It has a Boc-protected piperazine
- It has a cyclobutane-fused tetrahydropyran ring system
- It has a fluorophenyl sulfonyl group
- The flavanone ring system needs to be disconnected first, then the ketone oxidized back, the bromine removed, the piperazine nucleophile disconnected, and finally the nitro group restored before the sulfonamide coupling.

Let me reconsider the order. The hints describe forward reactions sequentially, so for retrosynthesis I'm working backwards through them. The target molecule contains a sulfonamide that forms in the final forward step, making it the first disconnection in retro. Working backwards through the sequence: the amine comes from reducing a nitro group, the aromatic nucleophile was introduced via substitution, the bromine was removed, the ketone was formed, and the chalcone precursor was cyclized to create the flavanone core.

Examining the structure more carefully, I see the fluorophenyl sulfonyl group attached to an NH on an aromatic ring, with a piperazine substituent bearing a Boc group, and a fused ring system containing a cyclobutane moiety.
